text:
maya: Heads up — spike in MFA push declines across multiple tenants, started ~00:32 UTC. Notifications from auth-alerts: high decline rate + user reports of repeated prompts. src ASN looks the same for multiple IPs. Anyone else seeing this?

sam: seeing it. auth-alerts #critical, 120+ declined pushes in 15m across 6 customers. ASN 39523. Pattern: low-and-slow, 1-2 pushes per user every ~30s.

jordan: query: 
```
// quick Kusto-like
AuthEvents
| where EventType == "MFA:Push" and Result == "Declined" and Timestamp > ago(30m)
| summarize count() by TenantId, SrcASN, SrcIP
```
Got tenant ids: t-18c, t-4f9, t-9b2 all hit.

eli: can we block ASN at perimeter for now? WAF has ASN block for 39523? Also pause push service for suspected tenants to stop fatigue.

maya: agree with block and session containment. Proposed containment: 1) Block ASN 39523 at WAF 2) Revoke all active sessions for affected tenants 3) Force re-auth (step-up) for all admin roles 4) Open incident channel and notify customer success.

sam: executed ASN block on WAF (rule id wf-773) — propagation ~30s. Revoke sessions: running script.

ops-bot: revoke-sessions --tenants t-18c,t-4f9,t-9b2 --reason "MFA push fatigue - suspected abuse" => started

jordan: FYI the push queue shows high retry count from our push provider for those tenants, suspect automated probe to cause fatigue.

eli: question: do session revokes invalidate SSO cookies immediately? We need to confirm KMS-signed session JWT invalidation behavior if key rotation not triggered.

maya: good call. Security note: revokes set exp property in session store and publish to sessions topic. But JWTs signed with old key might still be accepted until TTL unless we rotate signing key or add revocation list check. I'll escalate to infra.

sam: infra confirmed we have revocation checks for session ids on each auth. However some short-lived cookies are stateless JWTs with 5m TTL; revokes will block new token exchanges but existing JWTs may persist until expiry. We will force shorter TTL for affected tenants for next 24h.

eli: opened audit ticket to ensure all revocations logged: audit-1127. Also recommend we enable debug logging for push events for next 2h.

jordan: notify impacted customers: draft message ready. @customer-success to send. Also recommend immediate RBAC review for service accounts with MFA bypass flag.

maya: action items:
- customer-success: send notification and remediation steps
- infra: confirm revocation propagation + shorten JWT TTL for affected tenants (sam owns)
- eng-sec: add ASN throttle and push rate-limit per tenant (jordan owns)
- devex: add clearer docs for customers about how to opt into push-rate protections (eli owns)

eli: also propose post-incident: rotate SSO signing key in KMS and add automated revocation-list check for stateless tokens.

sam: putting rotation on the schedule, will coordinate with ops for no-downtime rotation.

ops-bot: revoke-sessions completed for t-18c,t-4f9,t-9b2. 2 admin accounts had active sessions that were revoked.

maya: closing initial containment — ASN block in place, sessions revoked, customers notified. Will keep thread for postmortem notes. :lock:

security-bot: incident created I-2026-2303 "MFA push fatigue - multi-tenant probes" assigned eng-sec.

jordan: quick note: consider adding anomaly rule for many distinct users in multiple tenants receiving pushes from same src_asn within short window.

eli: logging: saved log sample to S3 -> s3://redwood-incident-logs/1968501234/push-sample.log

maya: thanks all. we'll do a 30m follow-up and then schedule full postmortem.
